newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea worries about open interest in arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea worries about open interest in arbitrage.

text.p: The Securities Supervisory Board on Monday said it was concerned that increasing open interest for arbitrage trading between spot and futures trading would create volatility on the June settlement date.
"Unless the imbalance of open interest is eased, there is a possibility of big share price fluctuations on the settlement date on June 12," the board said in a statement.
As of June 7, the open interest for long spot shares was 2.04 million shares worth 28.9 billion won, up from 1.03 million shares worth 15.94 billion won at the end of May.
Open interest as of the same date for short June futures stood at 723 contracts worth 27.95 billion won, compared with 431 contracts worth 16.3 billion at the end of May.
Arbitrage is the simultaneous purchase and sale of the same or similar financial instruments with a view to making profits from the difference in prices.
The board said the increasing open interest for arbitrage trading was mainly due to an increase in the price of June futures compared to mid-May.
Futures are currently trading over theoretical prices, which provides investors with an opportunity to profit by buying spot stocks and selling futures.
Theoretical prices reflect the value level of specific futures contracts with consideration of current underlying assets.
The current situation recalls a plunge in share prices on December 12, the settlement date for December futures contracts, due to massive selling of shares for arbitrage trading.
As of December 7, the balance on December contracts stood at 1.417 billion won worth on spot trading and 1.432 billion won worth on December futures.
On December 12 last year the composite index fell 1.38 percent in after-hours trading.
